messages.text: Now can you also run Fatras single muon resolutions 1, 5, 10, 100 comparing track parameters of old and new baseline - using truth tracking

I’ll set up a matched old/new Fatras truth-tracking comparison at 1, 5, 10 and 100 GeV, using the existing reconstruction and resolution definitions. I’ll check the baseline inputs and run a small control before starting the full samples.

I’ll treat these as fixed pT values in GeV, with the established 3 T field and η range −4 to 4. The new baseline also needs hit-error calibration for its 2 mm strixels. I’ll check that independently before the fits. The environment registry still flags stale setup records, so the native control will verify the runtime directly.

The controls pass: all 100 old-baseline muons at 5 GeV fit successfully, and the new-baseline measurement-training pilot completed with its matching geometry and material map. I’m starting the full calibration and resolution samples, using the same truth-tracking chain for both baselines.

The new 2 mm calibration is complete and covers every measured sensor coordinate. The first full sample, old baseline at 1 GeV, also reproduces the previous run’s generated particles and fitted parameters exactly. The remaining cases are running; I’ll report fit losses and wrong-charge fits alongside the resolutions.

Both baselines have finished at 1 and 5 GeV; the 10 and 100 GeV samples are running. The first comparison shows mixed changes across track parameters. I’m keeping the full residual distributions and fit-loss accounting so the core-resolution plots can be interpreted properly.

The old 1 GeV sample reproduces the previous fitted parameters exactly. Centrally, the new baseline has a slightly narrower d₀ core, while its relative-pT core is about 13% wider. I’ll include an overview of new/old ratios alongside the per-momentum plots to make those tradeoffs visible.

The independent methodology review found no blocker to continuing. The analysis explicitly audits each case’s calibration and keeps failed or unavailable fits in the generated-event accounting. The old 10 GeV run is also complete; the remaining runs are progressing normally.

Both 10 GeV samples are complete. All eight samples were started fresh with the same frozen simulation and fit code; the 100 GeV pair is finishing now. The final plots will compare d₀, z₀, φ, θ, q/p and relative pT versus |η|, with fit-loss and charge-sign diagnostics alongside them.

The old 100 GeV run also reproduces its previous result exactly. It has substantial forward momentum tails and some wrong-charge fits, so a core width alone would be incomplete. Those outcomes remain in the comparison, and the report will show the full RMS and charge-sign counts. Only the new 100 GeV run remains.

The last sample has reached 19,000 of 20,000 events. Once it closes, I’ll check the output hashes, produce the final plots and get an independent check of the results. The forward 100 GeV diagnostics will stay visible alongside the core widths.

All eight runs are complete, and the final source, input, calibration and output checks pass. Centrally, the new baseline has narrower d₀ cores and wider relative-pT cores at all four momenta. I’ve produced the plots, ratio overview and full accounting report; they’re now ready for the independent results review.

Across the eight samples, 159,985 of 160,000 generated muons passed selection and produced finite fits; no attempted fit failed or returned invalid covariance. At 100 GeV, the charge-sign and tail diagnostics qualify the core-resolution comparison. The independent review is checking those details against the full ROOT samples and plots.

The independent review has reproduced the raw-data statistics and checked pairing, calibration variances, representative bootstrap intervals and all six plots. No material blocker has been found. The report also makes clear that the narrower new forward 100 GeV core comes with a much larger full RMS in this sample.

The independent review is complete and found no delivery blocker for this prototype comparison. It reproduced the full-sample statistics and calibration checks, including the forward-tail caveat. I’m recording the review and closing the reproducibility records; the plotted data are unchanged.

Completed **20,000 muons per baseline at fixed pT = 1, 5, 10, 100 GeV**, using Fatras truth tracking in 3 T.

Plots compare d₀, z₀, φ, θ, q/p and relative pT versus |η|:

[1 GeV]([redacted] · [5 GeV]([redacted] · [10 GeV]([redacted] · [100 GeV]([redacted]

Central d₀ improves; central relative-pT cores widen by roughly 6–13%. Forward at 100 GeV, the new core narrows while the full RMS grows substantially.

Eight tests and independent review passed. [Report, diagnostics and reproduction recipe]([redacted]
